bull_case: Nu has diversified retail deposits, substantial liquid assets, positive excess regulatory capital in every core country and high profitability. The franchise can fund growth internally while maintaining capital buffers.
bear_case: Deposit funding is largely short-term and the credit book is expanding rapidly. A severe regional credit/FX shock could hit asset quality, liquidity and capital simultaneously, while unused credit limits create large contingent exposure.
thesis: Financial survival is strong but the bank-specific balance sheet must be judged conservatively. Brazil CAR is 15.7% with $1.85B excess capital margin; Mexico and Colombia also exceed minimum capital ratios. Retail deposits dominate funding and liquid assets are substantial. The main mechanical penalty is off-balance credit commitments: $38.2B of unused limits are nearly 2x TTM revenue, while diluted shares are roughly flat YoY.

evidence.claim: At June 30, 2026 Brazil CET1 was 11.9%, Tier 1 13.4% and CAR 15.7%, with $1.848B excess margin; Mexico and Colombia capital ratios were 14.9% and 15.3%, each above 10.5% minima.
June 2026 financial assets included $13.55B cash, $19.18B securities and $9.15B compulsory/central-bank deposits, providing a substantial liquidity cushion against deposit funding.

Primary funding totaled $40.8B at June 30, with 87% from customer bank receipts/deposits and only 11% borrowings/financing; Nu monitors severe-stress liquidity daily and maintains contingency funding plans.
Unused credit-card limits were $38.164B at June 30, 2026. They are not fully expected liquidity needs but are off-balance credit exposure and roughly 1.97x estimated TTM accounting revenue.
Q2 2026 diluted weighted-average shares were 4.904837B versus 4.899768B in Q2 2025, an increase of only about 0.10% YoY; H1 repurchases totaled $500.4M.

counterevidence: Most deposit funding is contractually redeemable within 12 months, so confidence shocks matter.
Brazil CET1 and CAR declined from year-end 2025 as risk-weighted assets grew faster than capital.
The credit portfolio is expanding into higher-risk segments and 90+ NPL rose to 6.9%.
Unused credit limits increased materially, raising contingent ECL and stress exposure.
unknowns: Liquidity-buffer performance under a simultaneous Brazil/Mexico depositor and credit stress.
Capital consumption after Mexico transitions to a full banking model.
Full-cycle loss rates on recently expanded higher-risk cohorts.
falsifiers: Capital ratios approach regulatory minima while credit growth remains high.
Retail deposit outflows force expensive wholesale funding or emergency capital actions.
Equity issuance becomes necessary to support ordinary credit growth or absorb losses.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Nu is profitable, deposit-funded and above regulatory capital minima with positive excess capital; ordinary operations do not require recurrent equity funding.
Diluted shares increased only about 0.1% YoY and the company is actively repurchasing stock, so long-duration excessive dilution is not present.

subscores.rationale: Nu has strong liquid assets, diversified retail deposits and meaningful capital buffers. The score is above the 75 strong-liquidity anchor but below 90 because deposit funding is short-duration and capital ratios declined as RWA grew.

High profitability, daily stress-liquidity monitoring and excess regulatory capital support survival through stress, but a correlated regional credit/deposit shock would still require balance-sheet moderation.
Dilution is only about +0.1% YoY, mapping to the 0-3% row. Unused credit commitments are about 1.97x TTM revenue, also mapping to the 1-2x row. The rubric takes the lower axis, so 55.

uncertainties.rationale: Bank liquidity depends on depositor behavior and regulatory definitions rather than simple cash-minus-debt.
Current capital is strong, but recent higher-risk lending cohorts have not seasoned through a severe credit cycle.
Unused credit limits are ordinary banking commitments and not equivalent to industrial purchase obligations, but the locked rubric still penalizes their size mechanically.

dilution_metrics.rationale: Diluted shares are effectively flat. The H1 2026 buyback further supports the conclusion that equity issuance is not structurally funding growth.
